cells.tense: You're here at the bench with the pen in your hand.
cells.verb: building deep, each pass finer than the last
cells.place: inside the whole of it, seeing how every layer fits
cells.ask: offer one more round of the practice than feels safe — not to prove anything, just to let the refinement keep feeding itself, and notice that the quiet around you is connection, not distance.
cells.core: You're at the bench and you know it — not grinding, not performing, just working. What you make comes out finer each time because you stay with it, and you can see how the whole thing fits together while you're still inside it. The steadiness isn't strain. It's the work doing what it does when you let it.
cells.sheetLine: You're building it well, and the quiet is part of it.

cells.tense: You're braced for a bench that isn't here yet.
cells.verb: pushing the craft past where it's actually at
cells.place: trying to see the whole pattern before it's shaped enough to have one
cells.ask: take one finished pass and simply share it — let someone feel what you've been making and let the joy of it be the point, not the proof; what you're chasing arrives when the building is met, not when it's mastered.
cells.core: You've got the whole pattern in your head and you're working backward from it — every pass has to reach the version you're already picturing, and none of them do yet. So the bench has stopped being a place you're at and become a place you're failing to arrive at. The pushing is costing you the thing pushing was for.
cells.sheetLine: You're working toward a version nobody's asked you for yet.

lint.detail: the tense sentence does not read as Too Much's time

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding back the craft that's ready in you
cells.place: waiting to see the pattern before you'll trust it
cells.ask: say plainly what you already know about the shape of this — one clear declaration to one person, as if the pattern were already yours to name, because the structure that serves what it organizes is what things make sense in your presence again.
cells.core: You've stopped building. Somewhere back there the last pass didn't land the way you needed it to, and you've been waiting to be sure before you start again — but certainty isn't coming from where you're standing. The skill is still in your hands. The bench is just cold.
cells.sheetLine: The craft is ready and you've quit showing up to it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing in.
cells.verb: shaping the pattern without saying you're the one shaping it
cells.place: seeing it all clearly and calling it just how things are
cells.ask: notice one thing you've been building and say out loud that it's yours — not the craft's, not the moment's — and let the direction come from what you actually feel about it rather than from the thing that seems to be running on its own.
cells.core: You already see the whole thing — that's not in question. What you haven't said is that you're the one who built it. Your hands are on it, your decisions are in it, and you talk about it like it assembled itself while you happened to be nearby. The making is happening. Your name on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping this. You just haven't signed it.
